title: [RPG Design Guides] What Makes Players Want to See a Game Through?

blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】クリアしたくなるゲームデザインとは？
blocks.translation: [RPG Design Guides] What Makes Players Want to See a Game Through?

blocks.source: そこでどのようなゲームデザインをすれば、プレイヤーがクリアしたくなるかを考えてみたい。
blocks.translation: So, I would like to consider what kind of game design makes players want to see a game through.

blocks.source: 『クリアしたくなるゲームデザイン』となると、いわゆる『ヌルゲー』を想像されるかもしれない。けれど、ここで考えるのは難易度ばかりではない。
blocks.translation: When you hear “game design that makes players want to see a game through,” you might imagine what is commonly called an “easy game.” However, difficulty is not the only thing I want to consider here.

blocks.source: むしろ、初心者から上級者までを満足させるゲームデザインを考えていきたい次第。
blocks.translation: Rather, I would like to consider game design that satisfies everyone from beginners to advanced players.

blocks.source: ※ところどころ過去に書いた内容と重複してしまいましたが、そこはおさらいと思ってご容赦ください。
blocks.translation: ※Some parts overlap with things I have written in the past, but please consider them a review and forgive the repetition.

blocks.source: プレイヤーが投げ出す理由
blocks.translation: Why Players Give Up

blocks.source: まずはプレイヤーがなぜクリアせずに投げ出すかを考えてみる。
blocks.translation: First, let’s consider why players give up without seeing a game through.

blocks.source: クリアできずに、心が折れた
blocks.translation: They could not clear it and lost heart

blocks.source: 戦闘、ストーリなどを含めてテンポが悪い
blocks.translation: The pacing is poor, including the battles and story

blocks.source: 要するに面倒くさくて、我慢してまでクリアする動機がない。
blocks.translation: In short, it is too much of a hassle, and there is no motivation to endure it just to clear the game.

blocks.source: 長くて終りが見えない
blocks.translation: It is too long, and the end is nowhere in sight

blocks.source: 後ろ髪を引かれて辛い
blocks.translation: It is painful to be left regretting what they missed

blocks.source: 要するに取り逃しなどのコンプ要素の見逃しについて。
blocks.translation: In short, overlooking completion elements such as items that can be missed.

blocks.source: 候補としては、こんなところだろうか。
blocks.translation: I suppose those would be the main possibilities.

blocks.source: この他にも「ストーリーやシステムが好みじゃない」という理由も当然あるだろうけど、当然取り扱わない。一記事で扱える範疇じゃありませんので。
blocks.translation: There are naturally other reasons, such as “I don’t like the story or systems,” but I will not address them here. They are beyond the scope of a single article.

blocks.source: 上の個別に対して、対策を考えてみた。
blocks.translation: I considered possible solutions for each of the points above.

blocks.source: クリアできずに、心が折れた
blocks.translation: They Could Not Clear It and Lost Heart

blocks.source: プレイヤーが作品をクリアしない理由は、クリアできないからである。
blocks.translation: The reason players do not clear a game is that they cannot clear it.

blocks.source: ……そのまんま過ぎて説明はいらないですね。
blocks.translation: ……That is so obvious it hardly needs explaining.

blocks.source: 実際のところ、大半のＲＰＧは時間さえかければクリアできるようになっている。アクションやパズルのように何度やってもクリアできないなんて状況は、そうそうあるものではない。
blocks.translation: In reality, most RPGs can be cleared as long as you put in enough time. Situations where you cannot clear a game no matter how many times you try, as with an action game or puzzle, are quite rare.

blocks.source: 凶悪といわれるファミコンのドラクエ２ですら、１０時間～２０時間と経験値稼ぎに耐えられるなら十分にクリアできるはず。
blocks.translation: Even the notoriously brutal Dragon Quest II on the Famicom should be perfectly beatable if you can endure spending ten to twenty hours grinding for experience.

blocks.source: ……にもかかわらず、これは『クリアできない』と思わせるＲＰＧは現に存在する。プレイヤーの心を折ってしまう何かが存在しているわけだ。
blocks.translation: ……And yet, there are RPGs that make you feel, “I can’t clear this.” In other words, something exists that breaks the player’s spirit.

blocks.source: では、どう対処すればいいのだろうか？
blocks.translation: So how should we deal with this?

blocks.source: 難易度を下げる
blocks.translation: Lower the Difficulty

blocks.source: 一番に考えられるのは、やはり戦闘や謎解きの難易度が高いということ。その難易度を下げるのも一つの手段となる。
blocks.translation: The first possibility that comes to mind is that the battles or puzzles are simply too difficult. Lowering that difficulty is one possible solution.

blocks.source: これについては、特に説明不要だと思う。
blocks.translation: I do not think this requires any particular explanation.

blocks.source: ただし、安易な解決法であることも否めない。
blocks.translation: However, it is also undeniably an easy solution.

blocks.source: そもそもプレイヤーが挫折するのは、本当に難易度が原因なのかも疑っておきたい。
blocks.translation: To begin with, I want to question whether difficulty is really the reason players give up.

blocks.source: 分かりやすい理由だけに、プレイヤーも制作者も「難しかったから」の一言で片付けてしまいがち。
blocks.translation: Because it is such an obvious explanation, both players and creators tend to dismiss the matter with the simple statement, “Because it was difficult.”
[Example]

blocks.source: プレイヤーの感想
blocks.translation: Player’s impression

blocks.source: 「ダンジョンに三時間もかかって大変だったので疲れてしまいました」
blocks.translation: “The dungeon took three hours and was so exhausting that I ended up tired.”

blocks.source: 制作者の解釈
blocks.translation: Creator’s interpretation

blocks.source: 「当作品は歯応えのある難易度になっているので、ライトユーザの方には難しかったかもしれません」
blocks.translation: “This game is designed to have a challenging difficulty, so it may have been difficult for casual players.”

blocks.source: 今の時代、ネット上などで制作者がプレイヤーの意見を受けて、反応を返すことは珍しくない。その中では、上記のような噛み合わないやり取りが展開されたりする。
blocks.translation: These days, it is not unusual for creators to receive players’ opinions online and respond to them. In such exchanges, mismatched conversations like the one above sometimes unfold.

blocks.source: ※昔、どっかの企業で見た記憶があります。
blocks.translation: ※I remember seeing something like this at some company a long time ago.

blocks.source: 上のような感想なら大抵の場合、『難しい』というより『面倒臭い』と表現したほうが正しい。
blocks.translation: In most cases, an impression like the one above would be more accurately described as “a hassle” rather than “difficult.”

blocks.source: 確かに『難しい』ゲームはプレイ時間が延びるため、『面倒臭い』傾向がある。しかし、言うまでもなく『難しい』と『面倒臭い』は別の概念。
blocks.translation: It is true that “difficult” games tend to be “a hassle” because they take longer to play. However, needless to say, “difficult” and “a hassle” are different concepts.

blocks.source: そして、
blocks.translation: And

blocks.source: プレイヤーが挫折する一番の理由は『面倒臭い』である
blocks.translation: I want to argue that the biggest reason players give up is that something is “a hassle”

blocks.source: ということを主張しておきたい。そこを見誤ると、見当違いな対策になってしまう。
blocks.translation: That is what I want to argue. If you misunderstand this point, you will end up taking measures that miss the mark.

blocks.source: 実際には「難しくても諦めずにクリアしたくなるゲーム」と「難しいのでさっさと投げたくなるゲーム」の差は歴然と存在する。
blocks.translation: In reality, there is an obvious difference between “a game that makes you want to clear it without giving up, even though it is difficult” and “a game you want to throw down immediately because it is difficult.”

blocks.source: プレイヤーもその差を理解できず感覚的に「投げ出したのは難しかったから」という結論を出しているだけかもしれない。
blocks.translation: Players may not understand the difference either, and may simply arrive at the intuitive conclusion that “I gave up because it was difficult.”

blocks.source: というわけで、この記事では難易度を下げる以外の方法も積極的に考えていきたい。
blocks.translation: For that reason, in this article I would like to actively consider methods other than lowering the difficulty.

blocks.source: 長時間プレイを台無しにしない
blocks.translation: Do Not Ruin Long Play Sessions

blocks.source: 長々とプレイした挙げ句に全滅。二時間前のセーブポイントからやり直し……。
blocks.translation: After playing for a long time, you are wiped out. Then you have to start over from a save point two hours earlier……

blocks.source: というのは、プレイヤーの心を最も折る展開であり、やはり避けたい。
blocks.translation: That is the kind of development most likely to break a player’s spirit, so it should be avoided.

blocks.source: 昔はＦＦ３とか女神異聞録ペルソナとか色々とあったけれど。昔は昔。一時間、二時間とセーブをさせないゲームデザインは、さすがに時代的にしんどいのではないかなと。
blocks.translation: There were plenty of games like Final Fantasy III and Revelations: Persona in the past. But the past is the past. A game design that prevents players from saving for an hour or two is probably too tough for the times we live in.

blocks.source: そもそも、全滅のペナルティが大きすぎると、制作者だって思いきった難易度にするのは難しくなる。やり直しが気軽にできるからこそ、サガシリーズのボスはあれだけ強くても成り立つわけで。
blocks.translation: In the first place, if the penalty for being wiped out is too severe, it also becomes difficult for creators to set a truly bold difficulty level. The bosses in the SaGa series can be that strong precisely because you can easily try again.

blocks.source: セーブポイントは頻繁（常時セーブできてもＯＫ）に、全滅時のペナルティは控えめを心がけてみよう。
blocks.translation: Try to provide save points frequently (it is also fine to allow saving at any time) and keep the penalty for being wiped out moderate.

blocks.source: 上級者を過度に優遇しない
blocks.translation: Do Not Overly Favor Experienced Players

blocks.source: 例えば少ないターンや低レベルでボスを倒すと、ボーナスを出すなどの手法を指している。
blocks.translation: For example, this refers to methods such as offering bonuses for defeating bosses in fewer turns or at a lower level.

blocks.source: これをやる上での問題は、それができない初心者ほど不利になっていくということ。
blocks.translation: The problem with this is that beginners who cannot do so are placed at an even greater disadvantage.

blocks.source: 特にボーナスの中身がレアアイテムだった場合、取り逃しが発生するという難点もある。これは長編ＲＰＧにおいて大変厳しい。
blocks.translation: If the bonus is a rare item in particular, players may also miss out on it. This is especially harsh in a long RPG.

blocks.source: 初心者冷遇の末に、心を折ってしまうのは避けたいところ。
blocks.translation: You want to avoid breaking players' spirits by treating beginners unfairly.

blocks.source: よくあるのは、戦闘不能のキャラには経験値を渡さない仕様になっている場合。戦闘不能者がよく出る初心者ほど経験値に困る傾向がある。ボスなどの強制戦闘で、大量に経験値を出す場合は要注意！
blocks.translation: A common example is a system that does not award experience points to incapacitated characters. Beginners, who are more likely to have characters become incapacitated, tend to struggle with experience points. Be especially careful when awarding large amounts of experience in forced battles, such as boss fights!

blocks.source: 上級者の優遇は、意図しないうちに成り立つこともある。
blocks.translation: Experienced players may also end up being favored unintentionally.

blocks.source: 例えば、強制戦闘のボスを撃破した際に大量の経験値を与えると、レベルの均一化が起こってしまう。
blocks.translation: For example, giving a large amount of experience for defeating a boss in a forced battle can cause the party's levels to become more uniform.

blocks.source: 中ボスの想定レベルが３０。撃破すると経験値２０００００
blocks.translation: The mid-boss's intended level is 30. Defeating it awards 200,000 experience points.

blocks.source: 大ボスの想定レベルが４０
blocks.translation: The main boss's intended level is 40.

blocks.source: ちょっと極端な例になるけれど、「上級者は中ボスをレベル２０で撃破」「初心者はレベル４０で撃破」できたとする。
blocks.translation: This is a somewhat extreme example, but suppose an experienced player can defeat the mid-boss at level 20, while a beginner can defeat it at level 40.

blocks.source: 経験値２０００００を入手した場合、ＤＱ３の経験値曲線を例にすると――
blocks.translation: If they obtain 200,000 experience points, using DQ3's experience curve as an example—

blocks.source: 上級者：レベル２０→３２にアップ
blocks.translation: Experienced player: Level 20 → reaches level 32

blocks.source: 初心者：レベル４０→４２にアップ
blocks.translation: Beginner: Level 40 → reaches level 42

blocks.source: となる。
blocks.translation: That is what happens.

blocks.source: 想定レベル－１０で中ボスを倒した上級者なら、レベル３２でも大ボスに挑めそう。
blocks.translation: An experienced player who defeats the mid-boss 10 levels below the intended level may be able to challenge the main boss at level 32.

blocks.source: 想定レベル＋１０で中ボスを倒した初心者は、レベル４２でも厳しい。長時間の経験値稼ぎが必要となりそう。
blocks.translation: A beginner who defeats the mid-boss 10 levels above the intended level will still have a hard time at level 42. They will likely need to spend a long time grinding for experience.

blocks.source: というように初心者に厳しいゲームバランスになってしまう。
blocks.translation: This results in game balance that is harsh on beginners.

blocks.source: もちろん、「強敵を倒した報酬が欲しい」という意見もあるだろうし、ボス戦の経験値を奮発するのも一つの選択だと思う。とはいえ、ザコ戦の経験値とあまりに格差をつけてしまうと厳しくなってしまうことには注意したい。
blocks.translation: Of course, some people may want a reward for defeating a powerful enemy, and generously awarding experience for boss battles is one possible choice. Even so, keep in mind that making the disparity with experience from regular enemy battles too large can make the game excessively difficult.

blocks.source: ちなみに、強制ではなく任意で戦うボスは別にどっちでもよいと思う。
blocks.translation: By the way, I think either approach is fine for bosses that players can choose to fight rather than being forced to fight.

blocks.source: 手詰まり感を抱かせない
blocks.translation: Do Not Make Players Feel Stuck

blocks.source: ボスが強くて難しい。
blocks.translation: The boss is too strong and difficult.

blocks.source: だが、パーティを強化しようにも、既に装備は整えてある。
blocks.translation: But the party is already equipped with the best available gear, so there is no way to strengthen it.

blocks.source: レベルを上げても、大して能力が上がらない。
blocks.translation: Even leveling up does not improve their abilities very much.

blocks.source: 手詰まりになった。さて、やめようか。
blocks.translation: I'm stuck. Should I just quit?

blocks.source: ……というようになって心が折れるパターンに心当たりがないだろうか。
blocks.translation: Have you ever found yourself losing heart in a situation like this?

blocks.source: 慣れたプレイヤーならば打開策が思いつくかもしれないが、初心者もそうとは限らない。
blocks.translation: An experienced player might think of a way to overcome the problem, but the same cannot necessarily be said of beginners.

blocks.source: というか、筆者はＲＰＧ上級者のつもりだけど、それでも心当たりはたくさんある。昔のドラクエ２みたいに取り得る戦術が少ないと起こりやすい。
blocks.translation: In fact, I consider myself an experienced RPG player, but I still have plenty of experience with this. It is more likely to happen when there are few viable tactics, as in the old Dragon Quest II.

blocks.source: 対策としては下二つが参考になると思う。
blocks.translation: I think the following two measures may be helpful.

blocks.source: 金の使い道を常に用意
blocks.translation: Always Provide Ways to Spend Money

blocks.source: 既に今購入できる最強装備をそろえているが、ボスに勝てない。
blocks.translation: You already have all the strongest equipment currently available for purchase, but you still cannot defeat the boss.

blocks.source: こうなると取れる手段が少なくなってしまう。それこそが手詰まり感を誘発する。
blocks.translation: When this happens, the options available to you become limited. That is what creates the feeling of being stuck.

blocks.source: 常に今以上にパーティを強化する手段を用意しておきたい。
blocks.translation: You should always provide ways to strengthen the party beyond its current capabilities.

blocks.source: ある程度インフレさせる
blocks.translation: Allow Some Degree of Inflation

blocks.source: 変化に乏しいと、パーティが強くなった感覚が得られない。
blocks.translation: If there is too little change, players will not feel that their party has grown stronger.

blocks.source: ボスが倒せない際に「パーティを強化すれば打開できるのは？」という実感が持てないと、プレイヤーは手詰まりを感じてしまう。
blocks.translation: When players cannot defeat a boss, they need to feel that strengthening the party will help them overcome it. Without that feeling, they will feel stuck.

blocks.source: そのためにも、数値のインフレ率はある程度高めておきたい。
blocks.translation: For that reason, you should make the rate of numerical inflation reasonably high.

blocks.source: もちろん、やり過ぎるとバランス調整が難しくなるので、按配は考えよう。
blocks.translation: Of course, going too far will make balance adjustments difficult, so consider the right degree carefully.

blocks.source: 謎解きは控えめに
blocks.translation: Keep Puzzles Moderate

blocks.source: 謎解きが解けない場合も、もちろんプレイヤーの心を折りやすい。
blocks.translation: Naturally, being unable to solve a puzzle can also easily break a player's spirit.

blocks.source: 戦闘、ストーリなどを含めてテンポが悪い
blocks.translation: Avoid Poor Pacing in Battles, the Story, and Other Areas

blocks.source: プレイヤーが挫折する一番の理由は『面倒臭い』である――というのは既に主張した通り。『面倒臭い』ゲームとはすなわちテンポが悪いゲームである。
blocks.translation: As I have already argued, the main reason players give up is that a game feels like a hassle. In other words, a game that feels like a hassle is a game with poor pacing.

blocks.source: これは『クリアできない』ではなく『クリアしたくならない』に近いだろうか。
blocks.translation: Perhaps this is less about being unable to clear the game and more about not wanting to clear it.

blocks.source: そこでその『面倒臭い』を改善する方法を考えていきたい。
blocks.translation: With that in mind, I would like to consider ways to improve that feeling of hassle.

blocks.source: ……といっても、過去に書いたような内容と被っているので割愛気味でいきます。
blocks.translation: That said, this overlaps with things I have written about in the past, so I will keep this section brief.

blocks.source: 戦闘テンポや快適性を重視
blocks.translation: Prioritize Battle Pacing and Comfort

blocks.source: 戦闘はスピーディに。エンカウント率はほどほどに。ロード時間は短く。レスポンスは良好に。
blocks.translation: Make battles fast-paced. Keep the encounter rate reasonable. Keep loading times short. Make the game responsive.

blocks.source: 説明不要。過去に散々書いた気がするので省略。
blocks.translation: No explanation is necessary. I feel like I have written extensively about this in the past, so I will leave it out.

blocks.source: システムはシンプルに
blocks.translation: Keep Systems Simple

blocks.source: システムが無駄に複雑になっていないかという点にも注意しておきたい。
blocks.translation: You should also pay attention to whether the systems have become needlessly complex.

blocks.source: 何をするにも、やたらと手順が多いゲームシステムは要注意。
blocks.translation: Be wary of game systems that require an excessive number of steps for everything.

blocks.source: 重要施設が遠いのもよろしくない。（ＰＳ４版ドラクエ１１のメダル女学園など）
blocks.translation: It is also undesirable when important facilities are located far away (such as the Medal Girl Academy in the PS4 version of Dragon Quest XI).

blocks.source: また、アイテムの数なども過剰に多いと煩雑になりやすい。時には要素を削る覚悟も必要となる。
blocks.translation: Similarly, having an excessive number of items and the like can easily make the game cumbersome. Sometimes you need to be prepared to cut features.

blocks.source: 物語をテンポよく進める
blocks.translation: Keep the Story Moving at a Good Pace

blocks.source: 文章が冗長ではないかを考えてみる。ゲームにおいては、小説のように長々と文章を書けばよいというものではない。
blocks.translation: Consider whether your writing is unnecessarily wordy. In a game, you cannot simply write long passages of text as you would in a novel.

blocks.source: また、ゲーム特有の問題として、やたらにウェイト（待ち時間）を挟まないことに注意したい。
blocks.translation: Also, as a problem specific to games, be careful not to insert waits (periods of waiting) excessively.

blocks.source: 時々『！』『？』『汗』などのアイコンを表示する度に、長めのウェイトを挟む作品があるけど、これは結構気になる。
blocks.translation: Some games insert a long wait every time they display an icon such as “!”, “?”, or “sweat.” This can be quite distracting.

blocks.source: ウェイトを１秒単位で大雑把に指定する人がたまにいるけど、オススメできない。テストプレイすればすぐに分かるけれど、１秒というのは意外と長いので。
blocks.translation: Some people occasionally specify waits roughly in one-second increments, but I cannot recommend it. You will realize it immediately during testing, since one second is surprisingly long.

blocks.source: 長くて終りが見えない
blocks.translation: Too Long, with No End in Sight

blocks.source: 長くて終わりが見えず、クリアまであと何十時間かかるか分からない。もういいかな――とプレイヤーが諦めてしまうパターン。
blocks.translation: The game is so long that the end is nowhere in sight, and players have no idea how many more dozen hours it will take to clear it. Eventually, they may simply give up and think, “Maybe I’ve had enough.”

blocks.source: 時間を忘れるほど熱中させられれば何も問題はないけれど、残念ながら現実はそう簡単にはいかず。序盤、中盤、終盤と隙がなく面白いＲＰＧなんてそうそうあるものではない。
blocks.translation: There is no problem if you can engross players so completely that they lose track of time, but unfortunately, reality is not that simple. There are not many RPGs that remain consistently engaging from beginning to middle to end.

blocks.source: いかにして、プレイヤーを最後までつなぎとめられるかを考えてみよう。
blocks.translation: Consider how you can keep players engaged until the very end.

blocks.source: クリア時間はほどほどに
blocks.translation: Keep the Completion Time Reasonable

blocks.source: これはもう、プレイ時間稼ぎをしないという一点に尽きる。物語は終わるべき時に終わらせよう。
blocks.translation: Ultimately, it comes down to one thing: do not pad the playtime. Bring the story to an end when it should end.

blocks.source: 「俺は千時間も制作にかけたんだから、プレイヤーだって十時間ぐらいは付き合うべきだ。それが多少面倒であっても」
blocks.translation: “I spent a thousand hours making this, so players should spend around ten hours playing it, even if it is a little tedious.”

blocks.source: ……みたいな思考になっていたら要注意！
blocks.translation: If you find yourself thinking along those lines, be careful!

blocks.source: そういう作者自身が通しのテストプレイをしていない――なんていうのは論外。きちんと最初から最後まで、なるべくユーザと同じ条件でプレイしよう。二週、三週と自分でクリアすれば、ユーザに面倒を強いることの愚を嫌でも悟るはず。
blocks.translation: It is out of the question for the creator to have never played through the game from start to finish. Play it properly from beginning to end, under conditions as close as possible to those of your users. If you clear it yourself two or three times, you should inevitably realize how foolish it is to impose tediousness on your users.

blocks.source: また、クリア後の隠し要素なども無理して作る必要はない。統計上、クリア後にまで手をつけるユーザは意外と少ない。（ＰＳのトロフィー機能を参照）
blocks.translation: You also do not need to force yourself to create post-game secrets and other optional content. Statistically, surprisingly few users go on to play after clearing the game (see the PlayStation trophy system).

blocks.source: もっとも、個人制作でそこまで長くなることは珍しいだろうけど。
blocks.translation: That said, it would be unusual for an individually produced game to become quite that long.

blocks.source: ストーリー進行に目安を作る
blocks.translation: Create Milestones for Story Progression

blocks.source: ダラダラと区切りなく話が続くのはしんどいというもの。
blocks.translation: It is exhausting when a story drags on and on without any breaks.

blocks.source: そこでストーリーが着実に終わりに向かっているという進展感を与える。
blocks.translation: Instead, give players a sense of progress—that the story is steadily moving toward its conclusion.

blocks.source: おつかいイベントやタライ回しばかりに頼らず、序盤や中盤にもある程度の山場を用意しておく。
blocks.translation: Rather than relying solely on fetch quests and errands that send players from one person to another, prepare some significant turning points in the early and middle portions as well.

blocks.source: あるいは『四天王との対決』とか、『７つのボールを集める』とか。数字で目安を作ると分かりやすいかもしれない。まあ、話の先が読みやすいという問題点もあるわけですが……。
blocks.translation: For example, “the confrontation with the Four Heavenly Kings” or “collecting the seven balls.” Creating milestones with numbers may make things easier to understand. Of course, that also makes it easier to predict where the story is going…

blocks.source: 後ろ髪を引かれて辛い
blocks.translation: The Pain of Regret

blocks.source: 売り払った初期装備の木刀が、実は最強武器の素材だった。
blocks.translation: The wooden sword from the starting equipment that you sold was actually a material for the strongest weapon.

blocks.source: 既に倒したボスから盗めるアイテムが、限定品だった。
blocks.translation: An item that could be stolen from a boss you had already defeated was limited-edition.

blocks.source: 選択肢を間違えたら、仲間にならなくなった。
blocks.translation: Choosing the wrong option meant that the character would no longer join your party.

blocks.source: どうです？ 最初からやり直したくなりませんか？
blocks.translation: Well? Don’t you feel like starting over from the beginning?

blocks.source: やり直すのは面倒なので、とりあえずそのままやるけれど、モヤモヤした気持ちになって、モチベが落ちませんか？
blocks.translation: Starting over is a hassle, so you continue for the time being, but doesn’t it leave you feeling unsettled and make you lose motivation?

blocks.source: 後ろ髪を引かれた状態でプレイを続けるのは辛いもの。
blocks.translation: It is painful to continue playing while feeling that you have unfinished business.

blocks.source: 結局、続ける気にもなれず、かといってやり直す気にもなれず、気がついたら中途放置していたなんてことも。
blocks.translation: In the end, you may neither feel like continuing nor starting over, and before you know it, you have abandoned the game partway through.

blocks.source: 対策はもちろん取り逃し要素を減らすこと。ドラクエシリーズなんかは毎回やっていることではある。
blocks.translation: The obvious solution is to reduce the number of missable elements. The Dragon Quest series does this every time.

blocks.source: もっとも、自由度が高くて分岐の多いゲームは仕方がない。個人的にはそういうゲームも好きなので、完全否定するつもりもない。ただそういう場合もある程度、一周にかかるプレイ時間を下げたほうが妥当かと思う。
blocks.translation: Of course, there is not much you can do about games with a high degree of freedom and many branches. Personally, I like those kinds of games too, so I do not intend to reject them outright. Even so, in such cases, I think it is reasonable to reduce the playtime required for a single playthrough to some extent.

blocks.source: それ以外だと、ストーリー的なことも問題になるかもしれない。
blocks.translation: Aside from that, story-related aspects may also cause problems.

blocks.source: 例えばヒロインが死亡するなどして、プレイヤーが何か選択を間違ったのではないか――と思わせるのも危うい。それがゲーム的には正解ルートの一本道であっても、辛いものは辛い。
blocks.translation: For example, it is risky to make players wonder whether they made the wrong choice because the heroine died or something similar happened. Even if it is a linear, correct route from a gameplay perspective, it can still be painful.

blocks.source: プレイヤーが気持ちよく先に進みたくなるようなシナリオを作るのも、一つの技術だと思う。
blocks.translation: I believe that creating a scenario that makes players want to move forward comfortably is also a skill.

blocks.source: とはいえ、さすがにそこまで気にするとシナリオが制約されてしまう。あくまで自分の趣味と要相談ではあるけれど。
blocks.translation: That said, if you worry about it to that extent, it will place constraints on the scenario. Ultimately, it is something you need to discuss with your own tastes.

lines.source: 『[[LINK_1]]市販ＲＰＧのクリア率[[/LINK_1]]』の記事で書いた通り、クリアまでゲームをやるプレイヤーは意外と少ない。

parts.source: 』の記事で書いた通り、クリアまでゲームをやるプレイヤーは意外と少ない。

lines.translation: As I wrote in the article “[[LINK_1]]The Completion Rate of Commercial RPGs[[/LINK_1]],” surprisingly few players play a game all the way to the end.

lines.source: 戦闘を重視したゲームにしたいならば、謎解きを削るのも一つの手。何でもかんでも盛り込んでしまうのは考えもの。もっとも、[[LINK_1]]過去の記事[[/LINK_1]]でも長々と書いたので割愛する。

parts.source: 戦闘を重視したゲームにしたいならば、謎解きを削るのも一つの手。何でもかんでも盛り込んでしまうのは考えもの。もっとも、
でも長々と書いたので割愛する。

lines.translation: If you want to make a game that emphasizes combat, cutting down on puzzles is one option. Trying to include everything under the sun may not be the best idea. In any case, I wrote about this at length in a [[LINK_1]]previous article[[/LINK_1]], so I will omit it here.
[[LINK_1]]> Return to the RPG Design Guides index[[/LINK_1]]

texts.そこでどのようなゲームデザインをすれば、プレイヤーがクリアしたくなるかを考えてみ: So, I would like to consider what kind of game design makes players want to see a game through.
texts.『クリアしたくなるゲームデザイン』となると、いわゆる『ヌルゲー』を想像されるかも: When you hear “game design that makes players want to see a game through,” you might imagine what is commonly called an “easy game.” However, difficulty is not the only thing I want to consider here.
texts.むしろ、初心者から上級者までを満足させるゲームデザインを考えていきたい次第。: Rather, I would like to consider game design that satisfies everyone from beginners to advanced players.
texts.※ところどころ過去に書いた内容と重複してしまいましたが、そこはおさらいと思ってご: ※Some parts overlap with things I have written in the past, but please consider them a review and forgive the repetition.
texts.まずはプレイヤーがなぜクリアせずに投げ出すかを考えてみる。: First, let’s consider why players give up without seeing a game through.
texts.クリアできずに、心が折れた: They Could Not Clear It and Lost Heart
texts.戦闘、ストーリなどを含めてテンポが悪い: Avoid Poor Pacing in Battles, the Story, and Other Areas
texts.要するに面倒くさくて、我慢してまでクリアする動機がない。: In short, it is too much of a hassle, and there is no motivation to endure it just to clear the game.
texts.長くて終りが見えない: Too Long, with No End in Sight
texts.要するに取り逃しなどのコンプ要素の見逃しについて。: In short, overlooking completion elements such as items that can be missed.
texts.候補としては、こんなところだろうか。: I suppose those would be the main possibilities.
texts.この他にも「ストーリーやシステムが好みじゃない」という理由も当然あるだろうけど、: There are naturally other reasons, such as “I don’t like the story or systems,” but I will not address them here. They are beyond the scope of a single article.
texts.上の個別に対して、対策を考えてみた。: I considered possible solutions for each of the points above.
texts.プレイヤーが作品をクリアしない理由は、クリアできないからである。: The reason players do not clear a game is that they cannot clear it.
texts.……そのまんま過ぎて説明はいらないですね。: ……That is so obvious it hardly needs explaining.
texts.実際のところ、大半のＲＰＧは時間さえかければクリアできるようになっている。アクシ: In reality, most RPGs can be cleared as long as you put in enough time. Situations where you cannot clear a game no matter how many times you try, as with an action game or puzzle, are quite rare.
texts.凶悪といわれるファミコンのドラクエ２ですら、１０時間～２０時間と経験値稼ぎに耐え: Even the notoriously brutal Dragon Quest II on the Famicom should be perfectly beatable if you can endure spending ten to twenty hours grinding for experience.
texts.……にもかかわらず、これは『クリアできない』と思わせるＲＰＧは現に存在する。プレ: ……And yet, there are RPGs that make you feel, “I can’t clear this.” In other words, something exists that breaks the player’s spirit.
texts.では、どう対処すればいいのだろうか？: So how should we deal with this?
texts.一番に考えられるのは、やはり戦闘や謎解きの難易度が高いということ。その難易度を下: The first possibility that comes to mind is that the battles or puzzles are simply too difficult. Lowering that difficulty is one possible solution.
texts.これについては、特に説明不要だと思う。: I do not think this requires any particular explanation.
texts.ただし、安易な解決法であることも否めない。: However, it is also undeniably an easy solution.
texts.そもそもプレイヤーが挫折するのは、本当に難易度が原因なのかも疑っておきたい。: To begin with, I want to question whether difficulty is really the reason players give up.
texts.分かりやすい理由だけに、プレイヤーも制作者も「難しかったから」の一言で片付けてし: Because it is such an obvious explanation, both players and creators tend to dismiss the matter with the simple statement, “Because it was difficult.”
texts.「ダンジョンに三時間もかかって大変だったので疲れてしまいました」: “The dungeon took three hours and was so exhausting that I ended up tired.”
texts.「当作品は歯応えのある難易度になっているので、ライトユーザの方には難しかったかも: “This game is designed to have a challenging difficulty, so it may have been difficult for casual players.”
texts.今の時代、ネット上などで制作者がプレイヤーの意見を受けて、反応を返すことは珍しく: These days, it is not unusual for creators to receive players’ opinions online and respond to them. In such exchanges, mismatched conversations like the one above sometimes unfold.
texts.※昔、どっかの企業で見た記憶があります。: ※I remember seeing something like this at some company a long time ago.
texts.上のような感想なら大抵の場合、『難しい』というより『面倒臭い』と表現したほうが正: In most cases, an impression like the one above would be more accurately described as “a hassle” rather than “difficult.”
texts.確かに『難しい』ゲームはプレイ時間が延びるため、『面倒臭い』傾向がある。しかし、: It is true that “difficult” games tend to be “a hassle” because they take longer to play. However, needless to say, “difficult” and “a hassle” are different concepts.
texts.プレイヤーが挫折する一番の理由は『面倒臭い』である: I want to argue that the biggest reason players give up is that something is “a hassle”
texts.ということを主張しておきたい。そこを見誤ると、見当違いな対策になってしまう。: That is what I want to argue. If you misunderstand this point, you will end up taking measures that miss the mark.
texts.実際には「難しくても諦めずにクリアしたくなるゲーム」と「難しいのでさっさと投げた: In reality, there is an obvious difference between “a game that makes you want to clear it without giving up, even though it is difficult” and “a game you want to throw down immediately because it is difficult.”
texts.プレイヤーもその差を理解できず感覚的に「投げ出したのは難しかったから」という結論: Players may not understand the difference either, and may simply arrive at the intuitive conclusion that “I gave up because it was difficult.”
texts.というわけで、この記事では難易度を下げる以外の方法も積極的に考えていきたい。: For that reason, in this article I would like to actively consider methods other than lowering the difficulty.
texts.長時間プレイを台無しにしない: Do Not Ruin Long Play Sessions
texts.長々とプレイした挙げ句に全滅。二時間前のセーブポイントからやり直し……。: After playing for a long time, you are wiped out. Then you have to start over from a save point two hours earlier……
texts.というのは、プレイヤーの心を最も折る展開であり、やはり避けたい。: That is the kind of development most likely to break a player’s spirit, so it should be avoided.
texts.昔はＦＦ３とか女神異聞録ペルソナとか色々とあったけれど。昔は昔。一時間、二時間と: There were plenty of games like Final Fantasy III and Revelations: Persona in the past. But the past is the past. A game design that prevents players from saving for an hour or two is probably too tough for the times we live in.
texts.そもそも、全滅のペナルティが大きすぎると、制作者だって思いきった難易度にするのは: In the first place, if the penalty for being wiped out is too severe, it also becomes difficult for creators to set a truly bold difficulty level. The bosses in the SaGa series can be that strong precisely because you can easily try again.
texts.セーブポイントは頻繁（常時セーブできてもＯＫ）に、全滅時のペナルティは控えめを心: Try to provide save points frequently (it is also fine to allow saving at any time) and keep the penalty for being wiped out moderate.
texts.上級者を過度に優遇しない: Do Not Overly Favor Experienced Players
texts.例えば少ないターンや低レベルでボスを倒すと、ボーナスを出すなどの手法を指している: For example, this refers to methods such as offering bonuses for defeating bosses in fewer turns or at a lower level.
texts.これをやる上での問題は、それができない初心者ほど不利になっていくということ。: The problem with this is that beginners who cannot do so are placed at an even greater disadvantage.
texts.特にボーナスの中身がレアアイテムだった場合、取り逃しが発生するという難点もある。: If the bonus is a rare item in particular, players may also miss out on it. This is especially harsh in a long RPG.
texts.初心者冷遇の末に、心を折ってしまうのは避けたいところ。: You want to avoid breaking players' spirits by treating beginners unfairly.
texts.よくあるのは、戦闘不能のキャラには経験値を渡さない仕様になっている場合。戦闘不能: A common example is a system that does not award experience points to incapacitated characters. Beginners, who are more likely to have characters become incapacitated, tend to struggle with experience points. Be especially careful when awarding large amounts of experience in forced battles, such as boss fights!
texts.上級者の優遇は、意図しないうちに成り立つこともある。: Experienced players may also end up being favored unintentionally.
texts.例えば、強制戦闘のボスを撃破した際に大量の経験値を与えると、レベルの均一化が起こ: For example, giving a large amount of experience for defeating a boss in a forced battle can cause the party's levels to become more uniform.
texts.中ボスの想定レベルが３０。撃破すると経験値２０００００: The mid-boss's intended level is 30. Defeating it awards 200,000 experience points.
texts.大ボスの想定レベルが４０: The main boss's intended level is 40.
texts.ちょっと極端な例になるけれど、「上級者は中ボスをレベル２０で撃破」「初心者はレベ: This is a somewhat extreme example, but suppose an experienced player can defeat the mid-boss at level 20, while a beginner can defeat it at level 40.
texts.経験値２０００００を入手した場合、ＤＱ３の経験値曲線を例にすると――: If they obtain 200,000 experience points, using DQ3's experience curve as an example—
texts.想定レベル－１０で中ボスを倒した上級者なら、レベル３２でも大ボスに挑めそう。: An experienced player who defeats the mid-boss 10 levels below the intended level may be able to challenge the main boss at level 32.
texts.想定レベル＋１０で中ボスを倒した初心者は、レベル４２でも厳しい。長時間の経験値稼: A beginner who defeats the mid-boss 10 levels above the intended level will still have a hard time at level 42. They will likely need to spend a long time grinding for experience.
texts.というように初心者に厳しいゲームバランスになってしまう。: This results in game balance that is harsh on beginners.
texts.もちろん、「強敵を倒した報酬が欲しい」という意見もあるだろうし、ボス戦の経験値を: Of course, some people may want a reward for defeating a powerful enemy, and generously awarding experience for boss battles is one possible choice. Even so, keep in mind that making the disparity with experience from regular enemy battles too large can make the game excessively difficult.
texts.ちなみに、強制ではなく任意で戦うボスは別にどっちでもよいと思う。: By the way, I think either approach is fine for bosses that players can choose to fight rather than being forced to fight.
texts.手詰まり感を抱かせない: Do Not Make Players Feel Stuck
texts.ボスが強くて難しい。: The boss is too strong and difficult.
texts.だが、パーティを強化しようにも、既に装備は整えてある。: But the party is already equipped with the best available gear, so there is no way to strengthen it.
texts.レベルを上げても、大して能力が上がらない。: Even leveling up does not improve their abilities very much.
texts.手詰まりになった。さて、やめようか。: I'm stuck. Should I just quit?
texts.……というようになって心が折れるパターンに心当たりがないだろうか。: Have you ever found yourself losing heart in a situation like this?
texts.慣れたプレイヤーならば打開策が思いつくかもしれないが、初心者もそうとは限らない。: An experienced player might think of a way to overcome the problem, but the same cannot necessarily be said of beginners.
texts.というか、筆者はＲＰＧ上級者のつもりだけど、それでも心当たりはたくさんある。昔の: In fact, I consider myself an experienced RPG player, but I still have plenty of experience with this. It is more likely to happen when there are few viable tactics, as in the old Dragon Quest II.
texts.対策としては下二つが参考になると思う。: I think the following two measures may be helpful.
texts.金の使い道を常に用意: Always Provide Ways to Spend Money
texts.既に今購入できる最強装備をそろえているが、ボスに勝てない。: You already have all the strongest equipment currently available for purchase, but you still cannot defeat the boss.
texts.こうなると取れる手段が少なくなってしまう。それこそが手詰まり感を誘発する。: When this happens, the options available to you become limited. That is what creates the feeling of being stuck.
texts.常に今以上にパーティを強化する手段を用意しておきたい。: You should always provide ways to strengthen the party beyond its current capabilities.
texts.変化に乏しいと、パーティが強くなった感覚が得られない。: If there is too little change, players will not feel that their party has grown stronger.
texts.ボスが倒せない際に「パーティを強化すれば打開できるのは？」という実感が持てないと: When players cannot defeat a boss, they need to feel that strengthening the party will help them overcome it. Without that feeling, they will feel stuck.
texts.そのためにも、数値のインフレ率はある程度高めておきたい。: For that reason, you should make the rate of numerical inflation reasonably high.
texts.もちろん、やり過ぎるとバランス調整が難しくなるので、按配は考えよう。: Of course, going too far will make balance adjustments difficult, so consider the right degree carefully.
texts.謎解きが解けない場合も、もちろんプレイヤーの心を折りやすい。: Naturally, being unable to solve a puzzle can also easily break a player's spirit.
texts.プレイヤーが挫折する一番の理由は『面倒臭い』である――というのは既に主張した通り: As I have already argued, the main reason players give up is that a game feels like a hassle. In other words, a game that feels like a hassle is a game with poor pacing.
texts.これは『クリアできない』ではなく『クリアしたくならない』に近いだろうか。: Perhaps this is less about being unable to clear the game and more about not wanting to clear it.
texts.そこでその『面倒臭い』を改善する方法を考えていきたい。: With that in mind, I would like to consider ways to improve that feeling of hassle.
texts.……といっても、過去に書いたような内容と被っているので割愛気味でいきます。: That said, this overlaps with things I have written about in the past, so I will keep this section brief.
texts.戦闘はスピーディに。エンカウント率はほどほどに。ロード時間は短く。レスポンスは良: Make battles fast-paced. Keep the encounter rate reasonable. Keep loading times short. Make the game responsive.
texts.説明不要。過去に散々書いた気がするので省略。: No explanation is necessary. I feel like I have written extensively about this in the past, so I will leave it out.
texts.システムが無駄に複雑になっていないかという点にも注意しておきたい。: You should also pay attention to whether the systems have become needlessly complex.
texts.何をするにも、やたらと手順が多いゲームシステムは要注意。: Be wary of game systems that require an excessive number of steps for everything.
texts.重要施設が遠いのもよろしくない。（ＰＳ４版ドラクエ１１のメダル女学園など）: It is also undesirable when important facilities are located far away (such as the Medal Girl Academy in the PS4 version of Dragon Quest XI).
texts.また、アイテムの数なども過剰に多いと煩雑になりやすい。時には要素を削る覚悟も必要: Similarly, having an excessive number of items and the like can easily make the game cumbersome. Sometimes you need to be prepared to cut features.
texts.物語をテンポよく進める: Keep the Story Moving at a Good Pace
texts.文章が冗長ではないかを考えてみる。ゲームにおいては、小説のように長々と文章を書け: Consider whether your writing is unnecessarily wordy. In a game, you cannot simply write long passages of text as you would in a novel.
texts.また、ゲーム特有の問題として、やたらにウェイト（待ち時間）を挟まないことに注意し: Also, as a problem specific to games, be careful not to insert waits (periods of waiting) excessively.
texts.時々『！』『？』『汗』などのアイコンを表示する度に、長めのウェイトを挟む作品があ: Some games insert a long wait every time they display an icon such as “!”, “?”, or “sweat.” This can be quite distracting.
texts.ウェイトを１秒単位で大雑把に指定する人がたまにいるけど、オススメできない。テスト: Some people occasionally specify waits roughly in one-second increments, but I cannot recommend it. You will realize it immediately during testing, since one second is surprisingly long.
texts.長くて終わりが見えず、クリアまであと何十時間かかるか分からない。もういいかな――: The game is so long that the end is nowhere in sight, and players have no idea how many more dozen hours it will take to clear it. Eventually, they may simply give up and think, “Maybe I’ve had enough.”
texts.時間を忘れるほど熱中させられれば何も問題はないけれど、残念ながら現実はそう簡単に: There is no problem if you can engross players so completely that they lose track of time, but unfortunately, reality is not that simple. There are not many RPGs that remain consistently engaging from beginning to middle to end.
texts.いかにして、プレイヤーを最後までつなぎとめられるかを考えてみよう。: Consider how you can keep players engaged until the very end.
texts.これはもう、プレイ時間稼ぎをしないという一点に尽きる。物語は終わるべき時に終わら: Ultimately, it comes down to one thing: do not pad the playtime. Bring the story to an end when it should end.
texts.「俺は千時間も制作にかけたんだから、プレイヤーだって十時間ぐらいは付き合うべきだ: “I spent a thousand hours making this, so players should spend around ten hours playing it, even if it is a little tedious.”
texts.……みたいな思考になっていたら要注意！: If you find yourself thinking along those lines, be careful!
texts.そういう作者自身が通しのテストプレイをしていない――なんていうのは論外。きちんと: It is out of the question for the creator to have never played through the game from start to finish. Play it properly from beginning to end, under conditions as close as possible to those of your users. If you clear it yourself two or three times, you should inevitably realize how foolish it is to impose tediousness on your users.
texts.また、クリア後の隠し要素なども無理して作る必要はない。統計上、クリア後にまで手を: You also do not need to force yourself to create post-game secrets and other optional content. Statistically, surprisingly few users go on to play after clearing the game (see the PlayStation trophy system).
texts.もっとも、個人制作でそこまで長くなることは珍しいだろうけど。: That said, it would be unusual for an individually produced game to become quite that long.
texts.ダラダラと区切りなく話が続くのはしんどいというもの。: It is exhausting when a story drags on and on without any breaks.
texts.そこでストーリーが着実に終わりに向かっているという進展感を与える。: Instead, give players a sense of progress—that the story is steadily moving toward its conclusion.
texts.おつかいイベントやタライ回しばかりに頼らず、序盤や中盤にもある程度の山場を用意し: Rather than relying solely on fetch quests and errands that send players from one person to another, prepare some significant turning points in the early and middle portions as well.
texts.あるいは『四天王との対決』とか、『７つのボールを集める』とか。数字で目安を作ると: For example, “the confrontation with the Four Heavenly Kings” or “collecting the seven balls.” Creating milestones with numbers may make things easier to understand. Of course, that also makes it easier to predict where the story is going…
texts.売り払った初期装備の木刀が、実は最強武器の素材だった。: The wooden sword from the starting equipment that you sold was actually a material for the strongest weapon.
texts.既に倒したボスから盗めるアイテムが、限定品だった。: An item that could be stolen from a boss you had already defeated was limited-edition.
texts.選択肢を間違えたら、仲間にならなくなった。: Choosing the wrong option meant that the character would no longer join your party.
texts.どうです？ 最初からやり直したくなりませんか？: Well? Don’t you feel like starting over from the beginning?
texts.やり直すのは面倒なので、とりあえずそのままやるけれど、モヤモヤした気持ちになって: Starting over is a hassle, so you continue for the time being, but doesn’t it leave you feeling unsettled and make you lose motivation?
texts.後ろ髪を引かれた状態でプレイを続けるのは辛いもの。: It is painful to continue playing while feeling that you have unfinished business.
texts.結局、続ける気にもなれず、かといってやり直す気にもなれず、気がついたら中途放置し: In the end, you may neither feel like continuing nor starting over, and before you know it, you have abandoned the game partway through.
texts.対策はもちろん取り逃し要素を減らすこと。ドラクエシリーズなんかは毎回やっているこ: The obvious solution is to reduce the number of missable elements. The Dragon Quest series does this every time.
texts.もっとも、自由度が高くて分岐の多いゲームは仕方がない。個人的にはそういうゲームも: Of course, there is not much you can do about games with a high degree of freedom and many branches. Personally, I like those kinds of games too, so I do not intend to reject them outright. Even so, in such cases, I think it is reasonable to reduce the playtime required for a single playthrough to some extent.
texts.それ以外だと、ストーリー的なことも問題になるかもしれない。: Aside from that, story-related aspects may also cause problems.
texts.例えばヒロインが死亡するなどして、プレイヤーが何か選択を間違ったのではないか――: For example, it is risky to make players wonder whether they made the wrong choice because the heroine died or something similar happened. Even if it is a linear, correct route from a gameplay perspective, it can still be painful.
texts.プレイヤーが気持ちよく先に進みたくなるようなシナリオを作るのも、一つの技術だと思: I believe that creating a scenario that makes players want to move forward comfortably is also a skill.
texts.とはいえ、さすがにそこまで気にするとシナリオが制約されてしまう。あくまで自分の趣: That said, if you worry about it to that extent, it will place constraints on the scenario. Ultimately, it is something you need to discuss with your own tastes.
